LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ResetAll.Confirm: Put every Isekai Dungeons setting back to its default?
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.General.Intr: Switch whole features on or off, scale everything at once, or start from a preset.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Gates.Intro: Gates that tear open on your own colony map, unasked. They stay below your colony's rank. The guild's contracts are where the big expeditions come from.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Contracts.In: Dungeon work the guild posts out in the world: gates found before they open, breaks that already happened, and rescues on other factions' land.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Dungeons.Int: How every dungeon is built and filled: its layout, its fights, its room events and its decor. These apply to dungeons generated after the change.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Rewards.Intr: What a dungeon pays: the boss hoard, treasure rooms, chests and experience. The overall loot and experience multipliers are on the General tab.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Tower.Intro: The Tower of Gods, its summit, and the autopilot that grinds tower floors and clears gate dungeons.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Deep.Intro: Multi-floor dungeons the guild surveys, and what carries from one floor to the next inside them.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Interface.In: Presentation only. Nothing here changes difficulty or rewards.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Tab.Advanced.Int: The raw tables and internals the balance was built on. Changing these can throw off the pacing of the whole mod. Every value has a reset button.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Preset.Default.D: Every setting as the mod ships.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Preset.Relaxed.D: Fewer gates, longer countdowns, weaker rooms and slightly better loot.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Preset.Challengi: More gates and contracts, shorter countdowns, stronger and busier rooms.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Preset.Brutal.De: Gates every few days, breaches every 12 hours, packed rooms, higher local ranks and better pay.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Preset.TreasureH: Much richer hoards, more chests and rarer prizes, with slightly tougher rooms.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Preset.TowerOnly: Local gates, guild contracts and deep dungeon surveys all off. Just the climb.
A preset puts every setting back to default, then changes a few. Nothing happens until you confirm.
These apply everywhere and stack with the tower and deep dungeon multipliers.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LocalGatesEnable: Gates open on your colony map on their own schedule. Off stops new ones opening. Gates already open run their course.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GuildContractsEn: The guild posts dungeon contracts on the world map. Contracts already posted run their course.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerEnabled.Des: The tower rises early in the playthrough. Off stops it rising. A tower that already stands is never removed.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DeepDungeonsEnab: The guild reports multi-floor dungeons it has surveyed. Deep dungeons already on the planet stay.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GlobalEncounterM: Scales the creature budget of every dungeon room, breach, broken site, tower floor and deep floor. Higher means more and stronger creatures.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GlobalLootMultip: Scales the market value of every boss hoard and treasure room. Guaranteed mana cores are not affected.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GlobalXpMultipli: Scales the experience colonists get for clearing a dungeon or killing a boss that escaped one.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Gates.Ra: The top of the window comes from a table on the Advanced tab, looked up by your best colonist's rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Gates.Br: When the countdown runs out the dungeon empties onto your map in waves, and the gate stays open the whole time. The wave shares are on the Advanced tab.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GatesPerSeason.D: A season is 15 days. Gates keep their own schedule instead of competing with raids, so this number means what it says. At zero no gate opens on a schedule.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.FirstGateDay.Des: No scheduled gate opens before this day of the playthrough.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateIntervalJitt: How much the time between gates varies around the average, so they do not arrive like clockwork.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxActiveGatesPe: Open or breaching gates one colony map can hold. When the map is full, the next gate waits.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LocalRankShift.D: Moves the rank window of local gates up or down. A local gate still never goes above SSS.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LocalRankWindowS: How many ranks below the top of the window a local gate can roll. The top of the window is the most common result.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BreakTimerMultip: Scales how long a gate counts down before it breaches. Each dungeon type sets its own base time by rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.WarnHalfFraction: How far through the countdown the first warning letter arrives.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.FinalWarningHour: Hours before the breach that the last warning letter arrives. Off sends no final warning.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateCountdownLet: Send the half-way and final warning letters. The breach itself is always announced.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BreachWaveInterv: Hours between each wave of creatures leaving a breached gate.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BreachWaveLetter: Send a letter for every breach wave. The final wave, which brings the boss out, always sends one.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BreachXpRadius.D: Colonists this close to an escaped boss when it dies get the clear experience. If nobody is that close, the whole colony is paid.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ClearedCollapseH: How long a cleared dungeon must stay empty of your pawns before its gate closes.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.EjectStunSeconds: How long pawns are stunned when a collapsing or breaching dungeon throws them out.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Contract: A contract is never pitched above your best colonist, whatever these say.
Whatever is left over is an ordinary contract: a gate found before it opens, with a countdown to beat.
The finder's fee is paid on top of whatever the dungeon itself holds.
How many times per season (15 days) the guild posts work. Deep dungeon surveys come out of the same cycles. At zero the guild posts nothing.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.FirstQuestDay.De: The guild posts no dungeon work before this day.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.QuestIntervalJit: How much the time between contracts varies around the average.
Contracts the world map can hold at once. Beyond this the guild waits.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractRankShif: Moves the rank contracts centre on up or down. They still never go above your best colonist.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.CeilingChanceSol: Chance a contract reaches up to your best colonist's rank when nobody else is close to that rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.CeilingChanceNor: The same chance for a colony with a few colonists near the top.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.CeilingChanceDee: The same chance for a colony with a full expedition roster near the top.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AtCeilingShare.D: When a contract reaches up, how often it lands exactly on your best rank rather than somewhere between.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DeepBenchCount.D: Colonists within one rank of your best that count as a full expedition roster.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChancePostedBrok: Chance a new contract is a gate that has already broken open, with creatures loose around it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChancePostedResc: Chance a new contract is a break on another faction's land, with their defenders holding the line.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractDistance: Scales how far away contracts are posted. Higher ranks are always sent farther.
How long a posted gate waits before it tears open by itself. It then turns into a broken contract instead of disappearing.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BrokenSiteDays.D: How long a broken site stays on the world map before the guild writes it off.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractFeeMulti: Scales the silver the guild pays for a completed contract.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BrokenFeeMultipl: Extra fee multiplier for clearing a broken or rescue site.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RescueGoodwill.D: Goodwill gained with the faction whose land you cleared.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RescueFailureGoo: Goodwill lost when a break on a faction's land is left to run its course.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BrokenSurfaceSha: Share of the dungeon's creatures already on the surface when you arrive at a broken site.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BrokenScatterRad: How far from the torn gate the loose creatures are spread.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DefenderRingRadi: How far from the gate a rescued faction's defenders hold.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Dungeons: Tower and deep dungeon floors are rebuilt on every visit, so these also reshape floors you have already seen.
A treasure room with a live, rank-matched creature standing over the pile. Take it, tame it, or leave it alone.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MapSizeMultiplie: Scales every dungeon, tower floor and deep floor map. Bigger maps cost more performance.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RoomCountMultipl: Scales how many combat rooms a dungeon has, up to 16.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TreasureRoomsShi: Adds or removes treasure side rooms from each dungeon's own roll. Tower floors that set their own treasure count keep it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ShortcutMultipli: Scales the extra corridors that link rooms out of order and give high-rank dungeons loops to flank and fall back through.
Lengthens or shortens the longest optional branch a dungeon can grow. A wing always has at least one room.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxWingRoomsPerD: Total rooms all the optional branches of one dungeon may use.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.FirstRoomBudgetF: Creature budget of the first combat room, as a multiple of the rank's room budget.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LastRoomBudgetFa: Creature budget of the deepest combat room. Rooms between ramp from first to last, and no side room goes above this.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.OffPathBudgetFac: Budget multiplier for fights on side wings the party can walk past.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChampionBudgetFa: Budget multiplier for the room guarding a wing's treasure.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RoomTierRampDept: How many ranks below the gate the first room's creatures sit. The last room is always at the gate's own rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxCreaturesPerR: A hard cap on creatures in one room, whatever the budget allows. Keeps high ranks readable and the game fast.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BossMinionsMin.D: Fewest creatures that guard the boss.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BossMinionsMax.D: Most creatures that guard the boss.
How far an idle creature in an open-field dungeon may wander from its zone before it walks back.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.EventRoomFractio: Share of a dungeon's main-path rooms that can become room events such as ambushes, traps or guarded hoards.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MinPlainRooms.De: Rooms that always stay ordinary fights, however many events are allowed.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BeastVaultMinRan: Lowest gate rank whose treasure rooms can hold a beast.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BeastVaultChance: Chance a treasure room holds a beast at the lowest rank that allows one.
The chance at Nation rank. Ranks between are interpolated.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DungeonDreadEnab: Colonists inside a dungeon that is still alive get a mood penalty that grows with its rank. The other dungeon moods follow Isekai Leveling's mood setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorEnabled.Des: Dress dungeons with torches, statues, furniture and worked stone that grow richer with rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorDensityMult: Scales how much decor every room gets.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorEntryFactor: Decor multiplier for the room you arrive in.
Decor multiplier for the boss room.
Decor multiplier at the start of the dungeon.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorDepthEnd.De: Decor multiplier in the deepest rooms. Rooms between are interpolated.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorRefineFloor: Carved dungeons get rough-hewn and then smooth stone floors as rank rises.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorSmoothWalls: Carved dungeons get smoothed rock walls at higher ranks.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorCorridorTor: Light the corridors of higher-rank dungeons with torches.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.CorridorTorchSpa: Scales the distance between corridor torches. Higher means fewer torches.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorFireSpacing: Least distance between two fire lights in the same room.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorPlantFireDi: Least distance between glowing cave plants and fire. Cave plants die in any other light.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorAttemptsPer: Placement tries per room before it gives up. More tries fill crowded rooms better and generate a little slower.
What a hoard is made of
Spent in order: gear, runes, coin, relics, elixirs. Whatever is left becomes gold and mana cores.
Every clear pays one chest of its rank's grade. The extra chests and the rarity weights per grade are on the Advanced tab.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TreasureLootFrac: A treasure room's value as a share of the boss hoard's value.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.WingLootBonusPer: Extra treasure value for each additional room in the wing that leads to it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GearShare.Desc: Share of the hoard's value spent on weapons and armour. Two pieces are always included.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.CoinShare.Desc: Share of the hoard paid as loose coin.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RelicShare.Desc: Share of the hoard spent on relics, from D rank up.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxRelicShare.De: The priciest single relic, as a share of the hoard's value.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ElixirChance.Des: Chance an A-rank or better hoard includes elixirs.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TreasureGearChan: Chance a treasure room holds a weapon or piece of armour.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateScrollClearC: Chance a cleared dungeon's hoard includes a gate summoning scroll of the dungeon's rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateScrollTreasu: Chance a treasure room holds a gate summoning scroll of the dungeon's rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateScrollQuestC: Chance an Isekai hunt, bounty or creature quest adds a gate summoning scroll of the quest's rank to its reward.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ExtraChestChance: Scales the chance of extra lower-grade chests on top of the one every clear pays.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChestCommonWeigh: How likely a chest is to open on a common prize.
How likely a chest is to open on a rare prize.
How likely a chest is to open on an epic prize.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChestLegendaryWe: How likely a chest is to open on a legendary prize. Rarity also sets the prize's quality, refinement and rune chance.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChestHaulMessage: Name the chests a clear paid when it pays more than one.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ClearXpMultiplie: Dungeon clear experience as a multiple of the quest experience for the same rank. Every colonist inside gets it in full.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Tower.To: A floor's rank and size are fixed the first time anyone reaches it. The tower's rank and size curves are on the Advanced tab.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Tower.Au: Used by the auto-grind toggle on tower floors and the auto-clear toggle in gate dungeons.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerRaiseAfterS: Seconds of unpaused play after starting or loading a game before the tower appears. Also applies to existing saves that have no tower yet.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerEncounterMu: Encounter strength on tower floors, on top of the global setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerLootMultipl: Loot value on tower floors, on top of the global setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerXpMultiplie: Clear experience on tower floors, on top of the global setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerVillagersMi: Fewest villagers living on a market floor.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerVillagersMa: Most villagers living on a market floor.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GodhoodChangesAp: Ascending turns the hair white. Turning this off gives every ascended colonist their own hair colour back within seconds. Skin is never changed.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GodhoodHaloEnabl: Draw the halo over pawns who carry Godhood.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotFoodPau: Food level at which an autopilot pawn stops to eat, when nothing hostile is awake.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotRestPau: Rest level at which an autopilot pawn stops to sleep.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotFoodRes: Back to work after eating at
Food level that sends a paused pawn back to work. Always kept above the stopping level.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotRestRes: Back to work after sleeping at
Rest level that sends a paused pawn back to work. Always kept above the stopping level.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotRangedH: How far into their weapon's range ranged pawns walk before they hold position and fire.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotIdleTim: A paused pawn who is awake and not eating goes back to work after this long, so empty packs never stall the grind.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotSnoozeH: After a stop ends, the pawn cannot stop again for this long.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AutopilotDeferSe: How long the autopilot stands aside for an order it did not give, from you or from another mod, before it takes over again.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Deep.Beh: Each deep dungeon has one of these: the dead rise and follow you, creatures flee downward, the hive grows back, the depths go on alert, or the cold or the heat builds floor by floor.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ChancePostedDeep: Chance a guild cycle reports a deep dungeon instead of posting a contract. With contracts off, every cycle tries a survey.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxDeepDungeonsO: Most deep dungeons that can be on the world map at once.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DeepEncounterMul: Encounter strength on deep dungeon floors, on top of the global setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DeepLootMultipli: Loot value on deep dungeon floors, on top of the global setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DeepXpMultiplier: Clear experience on deep dungeon floors, on top of the global setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RisingDeadMax.De: Most corpses that rise and follow you down to the next floor.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RetreatMax.Desc: Most creatures that flee down to the next floor and wait for you there.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RegrowthMinShare: Share of a floor's creatures that grows back when you went only one floor past it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RegrowthMaxShare: Share that grows back once you went far enough past it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RegrowthFullAtDe: How many floors past a floor you must go before it grows back fully.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AlertPerFloor.De: Alert gained for each new floor you reach.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AlertPerDay.Desc: Alert gained for each day spent on a floor.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.AlertMaxShare.De: Extra creatures a floor gets at full alert, as a share of its normal population.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ColdFirstFloorTe: Temperature on the first floor of a cold dungeon.
Temperature on its deepest floor. Floors between are interpolated.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.HeatFirstFloorTe: Temperature on the first floor of a hot dungeon.
Temperature on its deepest floor. Floors between are interpolated.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Interfac: Isekai Leveling's soundtrack switch and volume still apply.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TitleCardEnabled: Show the dungeon's name and rank when you arrive.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateLabelsEnable: Show a gate's name and rank when you hover over it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateEffectsStren: Strength of the white light layered over gate portals.
How long the chest reel spins before it lands. The prize is decided before it starts, so closing the window early loses nothing.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DungeonMusicEnab: Play the dungeon themes while you are looking at a dungeon or tower floor.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MusicFadeOutSeco: Seconds the old track takes to fade away when a dungeon theme starts or ends.
Quiet between the old track and the new one.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MusicFadeInSecon: Seconds the new track takes to fade in.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerMusicSplitF: The last floor that plays the lower tower theme.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.Section.Advanced: One column per rank. Where a value is itself a rank, it is a number from 0 (F) to 9 (Nation).
Values between the listed points are interpolated.
Extra chests: each column is its own chance of one more chest, one grade lower each time. Use + and - to add or remove rolls. Rarity: relative weights, before the Rewards tab multipliers.
Each wave takes this share of whatever is still inside. The last wave always takes everything, the boss included.
Shorter poll intervals react faster and cost more.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LocalRankTopByCo: The highest rank a local gate can roll, by your best colonist's rank. Capped at 8 (SSS).
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractCentreOf: How many ranks below your best colonist contracts centre on, by that colonist's rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractMinTiles: Fewest world tiles away a contract of each rank is posted, before the travel distance setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractMaxTiles: Most world tiles away, before the travel distance setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractSilverBy: Silver the guild pays at each rank, before the finder's fee setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ContractGuildGoo: Goodwill with the Adventurers' Guild for completing a contract at each rank. Needs the Guild Faction add-on.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ClearXpBaseByRan: Base experience at each rank, before the clear experience premium.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ShortcutBudgetBy: Extra corridors a dungeon of each rank may add, before the shortcut setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxWingLengthByR: Longest optional branch at each rank, before the side wing setting.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RelicDrawsByRank: Expected relics per hoard. The whole part is guaranteed and the rest is a chance. F and E are zero on purpose: the only relic cheap enough there is one nobody can use yet.
Genes packed into a relic genepack at each rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorPointsByRan: Decor budget of a reference room at each rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerRankByFloor: Rank number at each floor, from 0 (F) to 8 (SSS). Only floors nobody has reached yet are affected.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.TowerMapSizeByFl: Map edge length at each floor, before the map size setting. Only floors nobody has reached yet are affected.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.CorridorTorchSpa: Cells between corridor torches at each decor level, from the lowest ranks to the highest. Zero means no torches.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.ExtraChestChance: Extra chests on a bronze clear
Chances of extra chests when a clear pays bronze (F to C). Nothing is below bronze, so its rolls repeat bronze.
Extra chests on a silver clear
Chances of extra chests when a clear pays silver (B and A).
Extra chests on a gold clear
Chances of extra chests when a clear pays gold (S and SS).
Extra chests on a jade clear
Chances of extra chests when a clear pays jade (SSS and Nation).
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RarityWeightsBro: Relative weight of each rarity in a bronze chest.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RarityWeightsSil: Relative weight of each rarity in a silver chest.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RarityWeightsGol: Relative weight of each rarity in a gold chest.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RarityWeightsJad: Relative weight of each rarity in a jade chest.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BreachWaveShares: Share of the creatures still inside that each wave takes, in order. The number of values is the number of waves.
Most main-path rooms one shortcut may bypass below S rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MaxShortcutSkipH: Rooms a shortcut may skip (S and up)
The same, at S rank and above.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.WingDepthStepFra: How much deeper each wing room counts, as a share of one main-path step. Deeper rooms get stronger creatures.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.OpenPackingEffic: Share of an open field's area its encounter zones may cover.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorReferenceAr: Room size in cells that gets exactly the rank's decor points. Bigger rooms get more, smaller ones less.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.DecorAreaFactorM: Least decor multiplier a small room gets for its size.
Most decor multiplier a large room gets for its size.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BeastVaultPickAt: Tries to find a tameable creature for a beast vault before giving up on it.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RosterRankMargin: How many ranks above the dungeon a themed creature or boss may be.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RosterRankFloorM: How many ranks below the dungeon a ranked creature may be.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.BackboneWeightFa: How often a dungeon of vanilla creatures is picked when themed dungeons exist at the same rank.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LootFallbackMult: Only used by a dungeon type that has no loot curve of its own, such as one from another mod.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.RelicSoftFloorSh: Relics worth less than this share of the hoard become less likely, so high ranks stop paying out trinkets.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.GateStateInterva: How often gates check their countdown and breach state. 60 ticks is one second at normal speed.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.MapStateInterval: How often a dungeon checks room aggro and whether it has been cleared.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.SuppressDungeonW: Stop the biome's wild animals wandering into dungeon maps. Turning this off lets them in, and every animal is another pawn to simulate.
LanguageData.IsekaiDungeons.Settings.LogGenerationSum: Write one line to the log for each generated layout and decor pass. Useful when reporting a bug.
